title: If Let It Be
goal: One interesting case, three ways to handle it. Pick the one with nothing extra.
hints: is_some() followed by unwrap() checks the shape twice - the pattern could have bound the value the first time.
if let is match for when only one arm matters.
explanation: check-then-unwrap asks 'is it Some?' and then asks AGAIN inside unwrap - Clippy's unnecessary_unwrap flags the double question, dropping it to Solved. The full match and if let both bind while testing and rank Optimal together - genuinely equal correctness; if let simply says it smaller when the None side is trivial. Rust often has two right answers; unwrap-after-checking is not one of them.
